fees.source: REPORTED - the county posts no nightly rate. https://thedyrt.com/camping/georgia/georgia-riverbend-park (camper review 'Reviewed Apr. 20, 2026': 'it's $5 a day paid via a drop box at the front') + https://www.n-georgia.com/southwest-georgia-parks.html ('Fees for Use of Boat Ramp and Primitive Camping - $5'); annual pass from https://img1.wsimg.com/blobby/go/9a5e215c-e768-4690-9491-3da4561aa591/RiverBend%20Pass%20Application.pdf ('BOATING & CAMPING . . . $150'), read 2026-10-30

sites.source: The site count (~10) and 25-ft maximum came from note prose resting only on Campendium camper reviews; the county's pages give neither, so they are cleared (read 2026-10-30).

note: Cusseta-Chattahoochee County park (not Stewart County) on Lake Walter F. George / the Chattahoochee River, west of US-27 off SR-53: a boat ramp with primitive camping along a gravel loop beside it. Camper reviews describe about 10 well-spaced drive-in sites with picnic tables and fire rings, pit toilets, a long gravel drive in, and a 25-ft truck camper fitting. --Claude
summary: The park belongs to the Unified Government of Cusseta-Chattahoochee County, not Stewart County: the county's Parks & Recreation page (phone 706-989-9911, matching the entry) links a 'Riverbend Annual Pass' form (Boating & Camping $150/yr); Google lists 'Riverbend Park' at 962 Riverbend Rd (4.4, 9 reviews). No county page gives a nightly rate or site details, so $5 is kept as reported (dated 2026 camper review), and the aggregator-only site count and 25-ft max are cleared. Imagery shows the ramp lot and a gravel loop with pull-offs; pin ~60 m from Google's point. Note rewritten.
flags: Website wrong: https://www.stewartcountyga.gov/ is Stewart County's home page (it doesn't load) - the operator is the Unified Government of Cusseta-Chattahoochee County: https://ugoccc.com/parks-and-recreation (the page Google Maps links for Riverbend Park). The county has no page for the campground itself.
Name: the county ('RIVERBEND ANNUAL PASS'), Google Maps and the n-georgia listing all call it 'Riverbend Park'; 'Riverbend County Park' appears only in directories.

Presence/inclusion: the county's only mention is the annual-pass form; current operation rests on Google Maps (4.4 stars, 9 reviews, no phone) and a 2026-04-20 camper review ('Quiet, well maintained park ... $5 a day paid via a drop box'). The Dyrt's summary calls it boat-in ('requires watercraft to reach the sites'), but its own site list shows 'Standard (Tent/RV)' and imagery shows drive-in pull-offs on a gravel loop - the boat-in wording looks like an AI-summary error. No source gives an RV length.
Open hours: n-georgia's listing says 'Open: Sunrise to sunset' for the park, which reads as day-use only; camper reviews describe overnight camping.
